title: Publication-Ready Figures for Cancer Bioinformatics
text: Publication-ready figures cancer bioinformatics, style lab submits . Kaplan-Meier curves hazard ratios, ROC time-dependent ROC curves, risk-score distributions, dimensionality-reduction projections, boxplots correlation plots, lasso coefficient paths, enrichment plots, immune-infiltration radar charts. Every function returns ggplot object, figures stay editable usual ggplot2 grammar.
code: library(gfplot)  p <- plot_KMCurve(clin, labels) gfplot_save(p, "figure1.png", width = 7, height = 5)

title: Publication-Ready Figures for Cancer Bioinformatics
text: Two problems come every manuscript. Figures drift apart, one tuned hand nothing matches. code produced lives one-scripts, next paper starts scratch. gfplot fixes second problem making figures functions, first opinionated presentation: Arial every figure. typeface journals ask , set default every function rather applied per plot. One baseline theme. Loading package sets ggplot2 theme cowplot::theme_cowplot(), every figure session starts look. Journal palettes. get_color() returns colour-blind-friendly palettes nature, jco, lancet, jama, jama_classic styles. deliberate choice, side effect. Attaching gfplot statement intended house style, package applies consistently. See Figure style change part .

title: Publication-Ready Figures for Cancer Bioinformatics
text: plot_forest() draws hazard ratios, odds ratios, mean differences confidence intervals numbers alongside. reads clinstats regression table directly, result goes model figure without reshaping: Ratios use log axis, halving doubling distance. Pass log_scale = FALSE effect measured difference, may legitimately cross zero.

title: Publication-Ready Figures for Cancer Bioinformatics
text: plot_ROC() answers whether model can rank patients. Three companion figures answer follows, usually harder question: plot_calibration() bins predictions quantiles draws binomial intervals, point rests similar number observations. plot_decision_curve() draws net benefit treating everyone treating one.

title: Publication-Ready Figures for Cancer Bioinformatics
text: gfplot_save() writes file graphics device can render figure font, chosen file extension. .png, .tiff, .jpg, .pdf supported. Use journal size preset produce figure width printed, rather scaling afterwards: explicit width height overrides preset dimension. Add provenance = TRUE write .provenance.json beside figure recording produced : record lets figure manuscript traced back code versions drew . Figures drawn printed, plot object turned file gfplot_save(), print(), ggsave().
code: gfplot_save(p, "figure1.png", width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300) gfplot_save(p, "figure1.pdf", width = 7, height = 5) gfplot_save(p, "figure2.png", size = "single")   # 85 mm, one column gfplot_save(p, "figure2.png", size = "onehalf")  # 114 mm, 1.5 columns gfplot_save(p, "figure2.png", size = "double")   # 170 mm, full width gfplot_save(p, "figure2.png", size = "slide")    # 16:9 presentation gfplot_save(p, "figure2.png", size = "double", provenance = TRUE) {   "schema": "gfplot.provenance.v1",   "figure": { "kind": "spec", "family": "forest" },   "output": { "format": "png", "width_in": 6.69, "sha256": "…" },   "environment": { "gfplot": "0.6.0", "r": "R version 4.6.0" } }

title: gfplot: publication-ready figures for cancer bioinformatics — gfplot-package
text: gfplot opinionated presentation. Figures use Arial cowplot::theme_cowplot() theme, lab standard publication output. Loading package therefore sets global ggplot2 theme theme_cowplot() session baseline: attaching gfplot statement style intended default, every figure session — including figures drawn packages — starts look. deliberate choice rather incidental side effect. Set options(gfplot.set_theme = FALSE) library(gfplot) keep existing theme; ggplot2::theme_set() can also called afterwards choose different baseline. Font colour follow principle. Arial default every plotting function, get_color() returns journal palettes, figures consistent across manuscript without per-figure tuning. See gfplot_save() writing files render font correctly.
